text:
anya: FYI new model nightingale-q4 is in canary. seeing a jump in funcall parse fails when batches split inside the JSON payload (~2.9% vs 0.8%). sample below.
harry: are we still using continuous-batching for that shard?
anya: yes. repro snippet from stream logs: 
```
INVOKE id=zz9 model=nightingale-q4 slice=18/64
OUT >> {\"tool\":\"db.search\",\"args\":{\"q\":\"chocolate croissant recipe\",\"k\":10}
...<stream cut>...
parse error: unexpected EOF
```
lui: looks like cut happened mid-JSON. smaller payloads fine. sometimes model emits a trailing "\n" or explicit sentinel and then parse succeeds.
qa-bot: canary summary: baseline 0.7% -> canary 2.9% over 1800 calls. top class: unexpected EOF (68%).
harry: hypothesis: quantization/token packing nudged token boundaries so the batch-slice deterministically cuts inside a token sequence that contains braces/commas.
anya: quick mitigations: (a) append a toolcall sentinel suffix to prompts, (b) widen batch-slice margin, (c) fallback json-repair heuristics on parse failures.
lui: can we flip a sentinel toggle in runtime and run a 1h micro-canary? perf hit acceptable for testing.
sre-bot: log collector: gathering 100 recent EOF examples -> /tmp/night-q4-eofs.tar.gz
harry: I'll prototype a lightweight first-chunk lint (unbalanced brackets, open string) to detect likely mid-JSON and either trigger a re-request or mark for graceful repair. cheap CPU.
anya: plan: (1) land runtime flag (off default), (2) enable for canary with smaller slices, (3) collect metrics: sentinel-accepted vs repair-applied, (4) if sentinel reduces failures >80% -> bake into batch cutter logic.
lui: tagging telemetry: "canary:nq4:sentinel" and "parse:repair_used".
anya: I'll post updates and dump raw failed payloads here as they arrive.
